The diplomatic salvo comes before a highly anticipated meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping when the US president is expected to attend the Apec conference in Shenzhen, China, on 18 and 19 November.

rfi.title: Democrats win US Congress in midterm rout of Trump
rfi.description: Democrats seized control of the US Congress on Tuesday, capturing the Senate and House of Representatives in a stunning, nationwide rejection of Donald Trump set to put the brakes on the final two years of his presidency.

rfi.title: French judges open inquiry into complaint of Israeli war crime
rfi.description: French judges have opened a judicial investigation into the complaint of a war crime following an Israeli strike on a residential building in Beirut in November 2024, it emerged on Tuesday.

rfi.title: Students blockade dozens of high schools in France before nationwide strike
rfi.description: Students blockaded dozens of high schools across France on Tuesday to maintain pressure on the government over education reforms as trade unions prepared for a nationwide strike later this week.

rfi.title: In Miami’s Little Haiti, ‘Blood’ looks past Trump’s rhetoric as US midterms loom
rfi.description: In Miami’s Little Haiti, a man mourning his mother and struggling to find steady work sees opportunity in Donald Trump’s politics. The president’s false claims about Haitian immigrants have not shaken his support. For the man known as Blood, what matters jus before the midterm elections is the promise of a chance to earn a living.

rfi.title: UN confirms start of process to wind up Western Sahara mission
rfi.description: The United Nations confirmed it had begun the process to end its peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara after Russia and the United States vetoed each other's draft resolutions on extending the 35-year-old deployment.

rfi.title: Nine out of 10 crimes against journalists go unpunished, Unesco says
rfi.description: Monday marks the International Day to End Impunity for Crimes Against Journalists – chosen in memory of Ghislaine Dupont and Claude Verlon, two journalists from Radio France Internationale who were murdered in Mali on 2 November, 2013. According to a report by Unesco, attacks and harassment targeting the press continue to go largely unpunished in Africa and across the globe.

rfi.title: French tennis star Fils starts bid for Paris Masters title and a spot in Turin
rfi.description: France's top tennis player Arthur Fils on Tuesday starts his bid for the Paris Masters title, and a place at the season-ending championships in Turin.

rfi.title: Calls mount to ban French TV channel following racist killing
rfi.description: A petition urging that a French television channel be taken off air gained traction on Monday, after accusations that far-right views it aired contributed to the racist killing of a black man.

rfi.title: Nigerian health chiefs confirm negative results in Ebola cases
rfi.description: Health authorities investigating two suspected Ebola cases in north-eastern Nigeria ​confirmed on Monday that both samples were negative after ‌two rounds of testing.

rfi.title: France braces for fresh protests as students to resume school blockades
rfi.description: France is readying for another week of protests after the head of a student group said a campaign of high school blockades would restart Monday, ahead of a nationwide day of strikes and protests on Thursday.

rfi.title: Miami voters weigh local hardship and America's global role as early voting ends
rfi.description: A massive thunderstorm and flash flood warnings failed to deter voters in Miami as they headed to polling stations on Florida’s final day of early voting ahead of the US midterm elections.

rfi.title: A year after the fall of El Fasher, Sudan's war has left a ghost town in its wake
rfi.description: A year after paramilitary forces at war with the Sudanese army captured the strategic city of El Fasher, survivors and aid workers report that the capital of North Darfur state remains largely abandoned. Some residents are too scared to return, while thousands are still missing – many held in deplorable conditions in overcrowded prisons.

rfi.title: France launches 'attempted murder' probe after petrol bomb attack on police
rfi.description: France has launched an attempted murder investigation after petrol bombs were thrown at security forces during a weekend protest in Paris, prosecutors told AFP on Sunday.

rfi.title: 'Working in Russia is like being a deep-sea diver', BBC's man in Moscow tells RFI
rfi.description: How does one report, from its capital, on the reality of Russia at war? Based in Moscow for more than 30 years, the BBC's Russia correspondent Steve Rosenberg is one of the few Western journalists still working in the country. He spoke to RFI about his daily life as a reporter in Russia and why he has chosen to stay, despite the Kremlin's increasing hostility to foreign media.

rfi.title: Five British anti-immigration activists arrested in northern France
rfi.description: French police say they've arrested five British far-right activists found carrying tear gas bombs, as they were filming themselves harassing migrants near the northern Channel port of Dunkirk.

rfi.title: 'Protecting the Congo's forests means protecting people's lives'
rfi.description: The forests of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo are a haven for some of the world's rarest species – but despite being protected areas, they are under threat from conflict, poaching and deforestation. After global decision-makers gathered at the United Nations' Cop17 biodiversity summit this week, Emmanuel Bahati Lukoo, a ranger at Kahuzi-Biega National Park, says people on the frontline of wildlife protection deserve greater recognition.

rfi.title: Why war makes Ukraine media more determined than ever to hold power to account
rfi.description: For Ukrainian media, exposing corruption in times of war is a high-stakes move – with domestic scandals potentially tarnishing the country's image in the eyes of the international partners it relies on. But journalists remain dedicated to their role as a counterbalance to the authorities, believing that upholding democracy is more important now than ever.

rfi.title: 'African leaders are not naive, they will partner with whoever makes the best offer’
rfi.description: The third Russia-Africa Summit took place in Moscow this week, with 48 African nations sending delegations. It comes as Moscow grapples with sanctions and isolation over its Ukraine offensive, while African governments turn to it for security assistance. However, geopolitical analyst Priyal Singh tells RFI that despite this, Russia still lags behind China in its influence on the continent.

euronews.title: Supermarket cyberattacks in Europe hit Italy's Coop stores in Catania and Palermo
euronews.description: On Monday night a cyberattack hit dozens of supermarkets in six European countries, raising fridge temperatures to 50°C and spoiling tonnes of food. Four Coop stores in Sicily were also damaged.

euronews.title: EU cancer groups fear funding squeeze under next long-term budget
euronews.description: As European Union countries negotiate funding allocations for the bloc’s next long-term budget, cancer organisations fear that projects spanning from research to personalised care and patient support could be discontinued, weakening cancer care across Europe.

euronews.title: US midterm elections: Cheers erupt as Talarico's Texas victory is projected
euronews.description: Supporters erupted in celebration in Austin as Democrat James Talarico was projected to win a US Senate seat in Texas, a state where his party has not won a Senate election since 1988.

euronews.title: 'He’s so strong': Former 007 actor Pierce Brosnan shares his pick for the next James Bond
euronews.description: The former Bond actor has given his seal of approval to 007 hopeful Callum Turner, who is rumoured to be one of the frontrunners for the coveted role. An official announcement regarding the identity of the next Bond is expected to drop before the end of the year.

euronews.title: 'Largest House majority' in decades, says election expert Boyd Wagner on US midterm elections
euronews.description:
Stefan Grobe speaks to Boyd Wagner, an elections expert on the surprise result of the US midterm elections.
The Democratic Party blew away expectations overnight, with historic results in long-time Republican states such as Kansas and Texas electing their first Democratic senators in decades.

euronews.title: Judicial crisis is 'weakening Poland' in a 'very unfortunate' time, says former EU Commissioner Jourová
euronews.description: Věra Jourová, former European Commissioner for Justice, believes this "judicial schism" is "very unpleasant" and "decreasing" the trust of Polish people in their justice and the independent judiciary system.

euronews.title: ‘We will take back the House in 2028’: US House Speaker Johnson promises Republican comeback
euronews.description: US House Speaker Mike Johnson has urged Republicans not to lose hope after Democrats made major gains in the 2026 midterm elections. Johnson vowed that Republicans would double down on their agenda and seek to retake the House in 2028.

euronews.title: 50 million Europeans can’t heat their homes. What is the EU doing to help?
euronews.description: Europe enters winter with its gas tanks emptier than at any point since 2011, and EU ministers have offered few binding answers on how to shield households from another energy shock. Watch the video!

euronews.title: ‘Democrats did a good job’: Trump congratulates Democrats on midterm wins
euronews.description: US President Donald Trump has acknowledged that rising petrol prices linked to the war in Iran contributed to his Republican Party's defeat in the midterm elections. He said voters supported his actions against Iran but were reluctant to pay more at the pump. Trump also praised Democrats.

euronews.title: Brussels to host talks on Ukraine's reconstruction with key allies
euronews.description: Good morning. I’m Mared Gwyn, holding the newsletter pen this Wednesday morning. Today: Brussels becomes the stage for intensified diplomacy on Ukraine, and I break down the key takeaways from Euronews’ Enlargement Summit.

euronews.title: Israel's election commission says no fraud found in last week's vote
euronews.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his supporters have repeatedly made unsubstantiated claims that Arab-led parties had “stolen” the election, possibly with foreign assistance.

euronews.title: US midterms: What Trump's defeat means for Europe and global markets
euronews.description: Democrats have won both chambers of the US Congress. For Europe, the big questions are tariffs and Ukraine, where Trump still holds much of his power.

euronews.title: Europe Today: Democrats win Senate in rebuke of Trump as Poland’s constitutional crisis drags on
euronews.description: A blue wave has swept the US in the midterm elections, with Democrats winning the Senate and heading for a big House majority as votes are still being counted on the West Coast. We bring live analysis from Philadelphia and Brussels, plus Poland’s crisis, Ukraine talks and the EU enlargement race.

euronews.title: Paul Krugman backs temporary rent caps to curb housing speculation in Europe
euronews.description: Paul Krugman says modern income-stabilisation models preserve construction incentives while easing a currently "impossible" situation. He also warns French public debt could be "catastrophic" and urges Europe to adopt "temporary protectionism".

euronews.title: ‘We defeated Goliath’: Talarico says after historic Texas Senate win
euronews.description: Democrat James Talarico has won the US Senate race in Texas, according to US media projections, marking a major breakthrough in a traditionally Republican state.

euronews.description: The first Black female governor, the first openly gay male senator and the first female Native American governor all won groundbreaking elections in the vote that racked up resounding wins for Democrats.

euronews.description: From castle backdrops to illuminated ice trails, these outdoor skating spots bring a little extra magic to a European winter break.

lemonde.title: Midterms 2026 : Donald Trump subit un revers historique
lemonde.description: La défaite brutale des républicains est d’abord liée au rejet du président américain, de son administration, de sa guerre en Iran avec Israël ou de la corruption institutionnalisée. Donald Trump n’a pas tenu compte des préoccupations des électeurs, qui s’inquiètent avant tout du coût de la vie.

lemonde.title: Midterms 2026 : James Talarico, le démocrate chrétien qui déclenche un séisme politique au Texas
lemonde.description: Ce séminariste de 37 ans a mis en avant sa foi pour séduire les électeurs modérés et remporter la bataille du Sénat, dans un Etat acquis aux républicains depuis des décennies. Les attaques contre son physique ou ses propos passés en faveur des minorités ne lui ont finalement pas porté tort.

lemonde.title: Budget 2027 : devant l’impasse des débats, Sébastien Lecornu explore la voie des ordonnances
lemonde.description: Alors que l’Assemblée nationale s’apprête à rejeter la partie recettes du projet de loi de finances, le gouvernement est soupçonné de laisser filer la discussion pour mettre en œuvre son texte initial par ordonnances, une solution jugée plus sûre que le recours au 49.3 par des membres du camp présidentiel, mais aussi de l’opposition.

lemonde.title: En Afrique du Sud, la déconfiture annoncée de l’ANC, en perte de vitesse dans les grandes villes du pays
lemonde.description: Chômage, criminalité, déliquescence des infrastructures, corruption… Le pays, dirigé depuis 1994 par le Congrès national africain, est rongé par de multiples crises. Le parti est annoncé au coude-à-coude avec l’Alliance démocratique lors du scrutin municipal de mercredi 4 novembre.

lemonde.title: L’incroyable essor des compléments alimentaires, porté par l’anxiété des Français
lemonde.description: Stress, troubles du sommeil, manque d’énergie, problèmes de digestion ou douleurs articulaires… Tous les prétextes sont bons pour prendre gélules, gouttes ou comprimés. Ce marché a triplé en quinze ans pour atteindre 3 milliards d’euros de chiffre d’affaires en France, attirant quelques grands groupes et une nuée de start-up.

lemonde.title: « Si tu tends l’oreille », de Yoshifumi Kondo : un film d’animation unique devenu légende
lemonde.description: Seule œuvre signée par le talentueux réalisateur, ce splendide conte réaliste, labellisé Ghibli, rencontra au Japon un succès phénoménal, lors de sa sortie en salle en 1995. Il nous parvient en France pour la première fois.

lemonde.title: Devant la commission d’enquête sur le 17 octobre, Laurent Nuñez reconnaît un « échec »
lemonde.description: Interrogé à l’Assemblée nationale, mardi 3 novembre, le ministre de l’intérieur a regretté un « défaut d’anticipation » des forces de l’ordre, « lié à la simultanéité des événements » lors des violences du 17 octobre.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Bruno Retailleau juge qu’il faudra une primaire en début d’année
lemonde.description: Le candidat Les Républicains disait, jusqu’à présent, ne pas s’opposer à une primaire, mais jugeait qu’elle ne pouvait avoir lieu en raison de la fin de non-recevoir d’Edouard Philippe, le mieux placé dans les sondages.

lemonde.title: Dans « Gouverner », Jordan Bardella creuse le sillon libéral-sécuritaire du RN, sans propositions nouvelles
lemonde.description: Dans son troisième livre en trois ans, le président du Rassemblement national, aspirant premier ministre de Marine Le Pen, multiplie les promesses de dérégulation et de baisses d’impôts aux milieux patronaux avant de se lancer dans une critique nourrie de l’Etat social.

lemonde.title: Route du Rhum : Armel Le Cléac’h a chaviré, quelques heures après Matthieu Perraut
lemonde.description: Le skippeur, qui occupait la deuxième place provisoire dans la catégorie Ultim, n’est pas blessé, a fait savoir la direction de la course. Depuis le départ dimanche de ce sprint océanique reliant Sain-Malo à Pointe-à-Puitre, plusieurs marins ont été contraints à l’abandon.

lemonde.title: Budget de la « Sécu » 2027 : le texte arrive au Sénat, après avoir été rejeté par les députés
lemonde.description: Faute de majorité, l’Assemblée nationale a dénaturé le texte avant de le rejeter. Le Sénat doit donc examiner la copie gouvernementale, sans savoir si le gouvernement choisira d’activer l’article 49.3 ou s’il préférera la voie inédite des ordonnances.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : 38 personnes pourraient encore être ensevelies sous les décombres de l’école bombardée lundi à Komychouvakha
lemonde.description: Ivan Fedorov, coprésident du conseil de défense de l’oblast de Zaporijia, a précisé que 31 corps avaient déjà été extraits et 12 identifiés. Selon les autorités ukrainiennes, l’abri aménagé dans une école a été touché par une bombe guidée de 3 tonnes alors qu’une distribution d’aide s’y déroulait.

lemonde.title: Au Masters 1000 de Paris, les adieux émouvants de Gaël Monfils au monde du tennis professionnel
lemonde.description: Le Francilien de 40 ans, qui a mis un terme il y a peu à sa carrière professionnelle, a reçu un vibrant hommage du public, mardi soir, pour l’ensemble de ses performances, mais aussi et surtout pour son charisme et sa générosité sur le court.

lemonde.title: Villarreal-PSG : une nouvelle démonstration des Parisiens, favoris à leur propre succession en Ligue des champions
lemonde.description: Le double tenant du titre a écrasé les Espagnols (6-0), mardi soir, en affichant une supériorité totale. En quête d’un troisième titre continental, Paris s’est rapproché d’une qualification directe pour les huitièmes de finale.

lemonde.title: Polluants éternels : 3M va verser 7,35 milliards de dollars de dédommagements

public-dom.description: In the late nineteenth century, visitors to Maine observed something strange: French-Canadian lumberjacks who, at the slightest stimulus, seemed to jump, strike out with their limbs, or mimic languages they could not speak. Ross Bullen introduces us to these so-called “Jumping Frenchmen” and to their greatest investigator, George M. Beard, who saw a link in their behavior between religious frenzy and neurasthenia.

public-dom.title: Rudolf Kalvach’s Wiener Werkstätte Postcards (1907)

public-dom.title: Paul Carus’ The History of the Devil and the Idea of Evil (1899)
public-dom.description: A history of the Evil One, from the earliest times to the present.

public-dom.title: The Alchemical Transformations of the Mutus Liber (1677)

public-dom.title: Philip Sidney and the Extreme (Dis)graces of the Parenthesis
public-dom.description: Erasmus called them “little moons” and George Puttenham praised them as “figures of tolerable disorder” (if used not too often “nor too thick”). For Philip Sidney, they were simply indispensable. Florence Hazrat introduces us to the uncontested early modern king of brackets and to his romance Arcadia, which abruptly ends, like its author’s life, hanging on a parenthesis.

public-dom.title: “There is Nothing but Immortality!”: Walt Whitman and The Book of Heavenly Death (1905)
public-dom.description: Choice excerpts from *Leaves of Grass* that speak to Whitman’s conception of immortality.

public-dom.title: Anatomy Unzipped: John of Arderne’s Sweden Scroll (ca. 1425–35)
public-dom.description: Early surgical diagrams that present patients prying themselves open for our anatomical gaze.

public-dom.title: In Company Style: Illustrations from James Skinner’s Kitāb-i tashrīḥ al-aqvām (1825)
public-dom.description: An illuminated Persian manuscript about customs, culture, and caste, written by an enigmatic figure of the early British Raj.

public-dom.title: Veronese's Dogs
public-dom.description: “Oh, if I could only pray”, Luther once said of his dog Tölpel, “the way this dog watches the meat”. Attending to attentive canine figures in half a dozen paintings by Paolo Veronese, Thomas W. Laqueur explores the work of an artist whose love of dogs landed him in hot water with the Inquisition.

public-dom.title: It’s “A Cat-astrophe”! (1919)
public-dom.description: “A Cat-astrophe” came on the tail end of an odd 1918 boom in cat-themed music.

public-dom.title: Metamorphosis: Transformations in the Early Modern Flap Book (early 19th century)
public-dom.description: By manipulating paper flaps, the child could turn Adam into Eve into a mermaid, a lion into a griffin into an eagle — all while learning about the inevitability of death.

public-dom.title: The Ties that Bind: Central Asian Ikat (ca. 19th century)
public-dom.description: Vibrant textiles from the dazzling Timurid metropolis of Bukhara.

public-dom.title: Artificial Intelligence: Ars Notoria and the Promise of Instant Knowledge
public-dom.description: Centuries before Neo instantly mastered Kung Fu in *The Matrix*, medieval scholars found a shortcut to years of difficult study: a magical manuscript that promised to fast-track advanced learning. Anne Lawrence-Mathers investigates the *Ars notoria*, its supposed powers, and the demonic influence it had upon some users.

public-dom.title: Photographs of Atlantic City Sand Sculpture (ca. 1880–1920)
public-dom.description: Photographs from when Atlantic City beaches featured artists ornately sculpting sand.

proj-syn.title: Oligarchic World Order
proj-syn.description: Today, some 64 heads of state or government are oligarchs, leading countries that together account for some 60% of global GDP. The question is thus no longer whether oligarchs will rule the world, but rather what kind of world they are building.

proj-syn.title: Poland’s Constitutional Civil War
proj-syn.description: Polish right-wing populists recently stormed the country's Constitutional Tribunal, winning applause from the Kremlin and far-right fellow-travelers across Europe. As in other countries, the constitutional tribunal is the institution that distinguishes a proper democracy from a dictatorship making it a target for authoritarians.

proj-syn.title: The Tech Brotherhood Wants Sovereignty
proj-syn.description: After centuries of nation-states, a new form of sovereignty is asserting itself. The small fraternity that controls the major digital platforms has already proven capable of even more intrusive and insidious forms of control than most states can muster.

proj-syn.title: The Far Right’s Vision for Europe
proj-syn.description: In many ways, Europe’s far right has already won, regardless of what happens at the ballot box in the coming months. Its parties may still quarrel among themselves, but they agree on the three big issues that will define much of the European political agenda for years to come.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Bright Future
proj-syn.description: A narrative of European decline has taken hold, and if the EU continues on its current path, it may well materialize. But this is not a foregone conclusion: Europe retains considerable strengths on which it can build as it pursues critical reforms aimed at unleashing innovation.

proj-syn.title: A Debtors’ Club for a Fragmented World
proj-syn.description: The newly created Borrowers’ Platform aims to facilitate knowledge-sharing and capacity-building among debtor countries, while amplifying their voices in global financial circles. But at a time when the Paris Club of sovereign creditors is increasingly unable to act collectively, the Borrowers’ Platform should ramp up its ambition.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Tariff Fiasco Could Save Free Trade
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump’s tariffs have raised prices and hurt businesses without reducing the trade deficit or creating manufacturing jobs. But global trade has held up better than expected, and growing public opposition to tariffs could pave the way for a retreat from protectionism.

proj-syn.title: If AI Thinks for Us, Democracy Will Suffer
proj-syn.description: Whereas the internet buried us in information, AI enables us to outsource analysis altogether. But when it comes to grappling with humanity’s most important questions, we must resist the temptation and recognize that we all have a duty—to each other and to ourselves—to keep “showing up.”

proj-syn.title: A Tory Mentor for the MAGA GOP
proj-syn.description: Kemi Badenoch’s keynote address at the British Conservative Party conference last month outlined her plan for a pro-growth future that respects fiscal discipline and human dignity. As American conservatives look beyond Donald Trump and to the 2028 primary campaign, they should embrace a similar agenda.

proj-syn.title: The Politics of Poland’s Judicial Crisis
proj-syn.description: The removal of Bogdan Święczkowski as president of the Constitutional Tribunal has triggered a physical confrontation at the court and a political standoff between Donald Tusk’s government and the far-right Law and Justice (PiS) party. But Święczkowski was not so much removed as barred, because he held the position illegally.

proj-syn.title: Mapping AI Resistance
proj-syn.description: Since a society that is reluctant to deploy a technology will not capture its gains, it is worth understanding why the AI revolution is being welcomed in some places and resisted in others. The explanation is not as simple as headline poll data and much media coverage suggest.

proj-syn.title: The World’s Perilous Ebola Complacency
proj-syn.description: The exponential trajectory of the latest Ebola outbreak is an urgent reminder that infectious diseases do not wait for ideal geopolitical alignments or balanced budgets. Global leaders must fund the Africa-led regional response today, or risk paying an immeasurably higher price in human lives and economic devastation tomorrow.

proj-syn.title: Industrial Decarbonization Is Good for Business
proj-syn.description: With major governments showing open hostility toward climate solutions or focusing on other needs, one might think that progress toward decarbonization is in jeopardy. Yet across the global industrial sector, many companies are increasing productivity, boosting revenue growth, and reducing emissions all at once.

proj-syn.title: When the AI Bubble Bursts
proj-syn.description: Speculative bubbles often leave behind valuable infrastructure while bankrupting the investors who financed them. AI could follow the same path, but the industry’s growing reliance on borrowed money raises the risk of a major financial crisis long before its world-beating applications emerge.

proj-syn.title: After Brazil and Serbia’s Elections
proj-syn.description: The recent electoral defeat of far-right forces in Brazil and Serbia offers important lessons for pro-democracy forces around the world as they confront nationalist and illiberal movements. But no single election can guarantee democracy’s resilience, and the challenges these countries’ new governments face remain formidable.

proj-syn.title: The New Geopolitics of Mining
proj-syn.description: While the US and China want their critical-mineral investments to deliver the biggest returns possible, governments in resource-rich countries must balance external pressures with internal demands. Mining firms must also win local communities’ trust, as host countries will be quick to throw them under the bus if public opinion sours.

proj-syn.title: Can Bond Vigilantes Prevent the Next Debt Crisis?
proj-syn.description: With interest rates on government debt having gone from near zero to much higher levels in recent years, rising short- and long-term bond yields have cast doubt on the sustainability of some debts and led many to wonder if a crisis might be looming. While some countries are more protected than others, none is immune.

crunchbase.title: China’s Largest Startup Deal Ever Lifts Global Venture Funding To $59B In October
crunchbase.description: Global venture funding in October totaled $59 billion, a 45% jump from a year earlier, per Crunchbase data, in large part due to a record-setting $15.9 billion funding round for China’s DeepSeek.

crunchbase.title: More Money, Fewer Checks: These 3 Charts Show The Divide Behind VC’s Record Funding Year
crunchbase.description: Record venture funding in 2026 has been increasingly concentrated in massive AI rounds, while seed- and early-stage deal counts are on the decline. Using Crunchbase data we provide a look at how third-quarter funding continued the year's dollars-up-but-deals-down trend.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Physical AI And Predictions Lead The Lineup
crunchbase.description: This week featured a robust lineup of large rounds, led by manufacturing startup Re:Build, which closed on $2.1 billion, and predictions marketplace Kalshi, which picked up another $1 billion.

crunchbase.title: Sector Snapshot: Travel Tech Funding Heads Toward Multiyear Low Despite AI Push
crunchbase.description: Travel demand appears to be holding up, but at the same time, investor appetite for travel tech startups has cooled. Even a wave of startups promising to improve travel with AI hasn’t managed to reverse the funding slowdown. We share what a review of Crunchbase data shows.

crunchbase.title: Series B Funding Is Up, But Fewer Deals Are Getting Done
crunchbase.description: Crunchbase data shows that so far this year, investors have poured around $48 billion into financings around the Series B stage, the highest tally in years. Yet round counts are below year-ago levels and are on track for a multiyear low. We take a look at the data.

crunchbase.title: Jumbo Series A Rounds Hiding The Real Squeeze On Seed Startups
crunchbase.description: AI megarounds are masking a shrinking Series A market, leaving seed founders facing higher revenue expectations and longer timelines despite larger seed checks. To improve their chances, MGV's Marc Schröder says, founders should size their seed funding around Series A milestones.

crunchbase.title: The Crunchbase Tech Layoffs Tracker
crunchbase.description: Over 127,000 workers at U.S.-based tech companies were laid off in mass job cuts in 2025, per a Crunchbase News tally, and the layoffs have continued into 2026. See the latest companies to cut roles.

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: Numeracle Raises $28M To Keep Legitimate Business Calls From Spam Label
crunchbase.description: Numeracle, a McLean, Virginia-based company that verifies businesses and links their identities to the phone numbers they use to contact customers, has raised $28 million from Edison Partners to help businesses whose calls are incorrectly labeled as spam or blocked by phone carriers.

crunchbase.title: The Invisible Graph: How Companies Grow Revenue And Still Lose Value
crunchbase.description: Revenue growth does not guarantee a larger exit, as declining valuation multiples can outweigh operating gains and reduce enterprise value. Guest author Itay Sagie suggests that founders and boards should track valuation alongside financial performance, model the effects of delaying a sale, and begin M&A preparation while the business is strong and buyer interest is favorable.

crunchbase.title: From Monk To Startups: One Founder’s Unusual Path To Building Government Software
crunchbase.description: After living as a monk while managing Graves’ disease, a former Facebook engineer left Big Tech to pursue meaningful work, eventually founding government software startup FSH Technologies which aims to improve processes such as school food services and public records management through the use of artificial intelligence.
